html:
A Turkic dynasty that ruled Central Asia from Kashgar to Samarkand between the 9th and early 13th centuries. It was the first Turkic state to make Islam its faith. The map shows it in 1100.

The turn came when its khan, Satuq Bughra Khan, became Muslim in the 10th century. In 999 the Kara-Khanids took Bukhara and ended the Samanids, bringing Turks to rule the old Persian cities of Transoxiana. The realm soon split into an eastern khanate, centred on Balasagun and Kashgar, and a western one around Samarkand.

Its courts produced the first great works in a Turkic language written in Arabic script: Yusuf of Balasagun's mirror for princes, the Kutadgu Bilig, and Mahmud al-Kashgari's dictionary of the Turkic tongues.

The khans became vassals of the Seljuks and then of the Qara Khitai, who beat the Seljuks at Qatwan in 1141. The Khwarazmshah ended the western line in 1212.
